https://news.worldcasinodirectory.com/ti.text: The Timişoara Local Council has approved a decision that will prevent gambling halls from receiving new authorizations in the city. The measure means existing venues can continue operating only until their licenses issued by national authorities expire, after which they will gradually close. Mayor Dominic Fritz announced the decision following Tuesday’s council meeting, stating that only National Lottery activities will continue to be authorized in Timişoara. “Starting today, gambling can no longer be authorized in the city. Only the National Lottery's lotto activities will operate in Timişoara. The current gaming halls that are still open in the city will operate until the licenses received from Bucharest expire, next year at the latest. Until then, they will close one by one. The fact that today we were able to decide what happens to the gaming halls in Timişoara is the merit of my USR parliamentary colleagues. They fought for years for this decision to be up to the local authorities. The Local Council made the decision unanimously,” Fritz said. The mayor added that the decision also reflects a responsibility toward residents and communities, highlighting the choice between allowing gambling venues to continue or directing resources toward education and public services. In spring, Timişoara had 173 locations authorized by the National Gambling Office for gambling activities. Existing Venues Will Remain Until Licenses Expire The council’s decision does not immediately shut down all gambling halls. Operators that already hold valid licenses can remain active until those approvals expire, with the final closures expected no later than 2027. The change follows years of discussions over whether local administrations should have greater authority over gambling locations. The city’s leadership credited parliamentary efforts that helped transfer more decision-making power to municipalities. Alfred Simonis, president of the Timiş County Council, previously announced financial incentives for local administrations that remove gambling halls. According to Simonis, municipalities that close such venues will receive funding for education-related projects. “Mayors who close gambling halls, gambling dens, as we know them, will receive money for schools. After the law that removed gambling from localities with under 15,000 inhabitants, the time has come for other communes and cities to eliminate them. (...). The money they will receive from the Timiş County Council will be allocated for the construction of new schools or kindergartens or for the modernization of existing ones,” Simonis explained, as reported by Stirile Pro TV. The funding plan is intended to support the construction of new educational facilities or improvements to existing ones. Local Restrictions Expand Across Romania Timişoara’s decision follows previous measures aimed at limiting gambling halls in smaller communities. Earlier legislation removed gambling activities from localities with fewer than 15,000 inhabitants, and local authorities in larger cities have continued discussions about additional restrictions. The Timişoara council’s unanimous vote gives the municipality control over future gambling authorizations within the city. Existing operators will remain subject to their current national licenses, but no new gambling halls will be approved. The decision comes as Romanian cities continue examining the role of gambling venues and their impact on local communities. Authorities have increasingly focused on regulating where such businesses can operate and redirecting attention toward alternative uses for commercial spaces.

https://www.zerohedge.com/geopolitical/p.text: ZeroHedge Reads Alt-Market AntiWar.com Bitcoin Magazine Bombthrower BULLIONSTAR Capitalist Exploits Christophe Barraud Dollar Collapse Dr. Housing Bubble Financial Revolutionist ForexLive Forum Geopolitica Gains Pains & Capital Gefira GMG Research Gold Core Implode-Explode Insider Paper Libertarian Institute Liberty Blitzkrieg Max Keiser Mises Institute Mish Talk Monetary Metals Newsquawk Of Two Minds Oil Price Open The Books Peter Schiff Portfolio Armor QTR’s Fringe Finance Safehaven Slope of Hope SpotGamma TF Metals Report The Automatic Earth The Burning Platform The Economic Populist Themis Trading Thoughtful Money Value Walk Visual Combat Banzai7 Wolf Street Expand Authored by Jill McLaughlin via The Epoch Times , Poland and Pentagon officials are in discussions about possibly locating several American military bases in the country, Polish Deputy Defense Minister Paweł Zalewski said after a meeting of the North Atlantic Council at NATO headquarters in Brussels Aug. 27. Zalewski said he met with Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby about plans for the bases and defense policy. "The American presence in Poland can encompass various defense capabilities," Zalewski told Polish Radio after the meeting. "We believe it doesn't have to be concentrated in one place. Of course, there are several locations we want to discuss with the U.S. side where such a presence would be truly massive. However, we are still talking about several bases and several locations." Poland formally requested new permanent U.S. military bases in June after Trump pledged to send 5,000 additional troops to the country. About 10,000 U.S. troops are already stationed in Poland, which spends about $15,000 for each, according to the country's defense department. Poland's priorities are to secure defense capabilities the country currently lacks, such as reconnaissance and command functions, rather than simply increasing troop numbers, Zalewski said. The bases would be a permanent strategy for the United States and not just a reaction to the ongoing conflict in Ukraine, according to Poland. "A permanent U.S. presence would reflect America's long-term strategic interest in the country, not merely respond to the recent activities of Russia," Zalewski said. The discussion also included nuclear weapons logistics, according to the deputy defense minister. He added, however, that Poland didn't want nuclear warheads stationed in the country. "Poland does not want to have nuclear warheads on this territory," Zalewski said. "We want to participate in NATO nuclear deterrence but that does not mean to have nuclear warheads on our territory." Poland's Minister of National Defense Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz appeared to clarify the comments in a statement on X later in the day. "To dispel any doubts: Poland remains steadfastly interested in participating in the NATO Nuclear Sharing program," Kosiniak-Kamysz said in the post. "We are also conducting talks regarding the proposal for participation in the European nuclear protective umbrella. Our government's stance on these issues is unequivocal." The Pentagon didn't respond to a request for comment about the bases by publication time. Colby visited Belgium this week to meet with European allies and press them to increase their defense expenditures as Washington evaluates its policy toward the region. The Pentagon asked the allies to assess their commitment to U.S. foreign policy goals as part of a European Force review launched in June by War Secretary Pete Hegseth. The review examines the future deployment of about 80,000 U.S. troops across Europe, with nearly half of them expected in Germany. Colby introduced the new framework, which he dubbed "NATO 3.0," earlier this year. Some countries are concerned the review will result in U.S. troop cuts in Europe. President Donald Trump has threatened to withdraw troops from countries that refused to help the United States secure the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran conflict. In May, the Pentagon ordered the withdrawal of 5,000 troops from Germany after tensions flared between Trump and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz over the Iran war. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said Friday that Europe and Canada had accepted a more equitable share of defense spending since last year. "Still, there is much more to be done and we'll get there," Rutte said. Magyar azt mondta, hogy az ukrán sajtóban terjedtek azok a hírek, hogy Magyarország is tagja a C8-nak, de „meghívtak minket, és mi jó okkal nem mentünk el.” Az ukrán elnök által korábban közzétett fotó alapján úgy tűnt, hogy Magyarország nem képviselteti magát az eseményen. Emiatt akkor megkerestük a Külügyminisztériumot, ahonnan a Telex kérdésére azt írták: a Kárpáti Nyolcak első csúcstalálkozóján, szeptember 18-án a kijevi magyar nagykövetség vezetője vett részt. Magyar most hétfőn a parlamentben azonban azt mondta: „Elég, hogy én vagyok a magyar miniszterelnök, és ha én nem tudok róla, akkor higgye el, Magyarország nem vesz részt ebben”. Azt is mondta, hogy „majd ha egyszer ebben Magyarország részt vesz, akkor bejelenti”. Volodimir Zelenszkij szerint a regionális együttműködési formátum célja, hogy közelebb hozza egymáshoz ezeket az országokat, és az uniós szinten is újabb együttműködési lehetőséget teremtsen. A tervek szerint a biztonság, az energia, a logisztika és a határokon átnyúló gazdasági együttműködés is a témák között lesz. Szerbiát Aleksandar Vučić elnök, Romániát Nicușor Dan elnök, Lengyelországot Donald Tusk miniszterelnök képviselte, Csehország és Ausztria egy-egy parlamenti politikust küldött, míg a több országnak nem volt jelen képviselője. http://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/27930.text: Big News Network.com Latvian welfare minister dismissed over drunk driving RIGA, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs on Sunday dismissed Welfare Minister Reinis Uzulnieks after he was detained by police on suspicion of drunk driving. According to the Latvian news agency LETA, police stopped Uzulnieks on Saturday night in Ropazi municipality near Riga. Two alcohol tests showed readings of 3.09 and nearly 3.5 per mille, far above the legal limit of 0.5 per mille for most drivers in Latvia. He was subsequently detained, and criminal proceedings were launched. Uzulnieks, 40, belongs to the Latvian Farmers' Union, a constituent party of the Greens and Farmers Union (ZZS), which is part of Latvia's governing coalition. Following the incident, ZZS held an emergency meeting on Sunday and withdrew its support for Uzulnieks as welfare minister. He was also expelled from the Latvian Farmers' Union. Kulbergs signed an order dismissing Uzulnieks and appointed Agriculture Minister Uldis Augulis as acting welfare minister. The prime minister said drunk driving endangers the lives and health of others and that such conduct by a government minister was unacceptable. Latvian President Edgars Rinkevics also condemned the incident, saying drunk driving by public officials was particularly unacceptable and should be punished in accordance with the law. "No one is above the law," he said. The incident comes just weeks before Latvia's parliamentary election on Oct. 3. Uzulnieks had been the top ZZS candidate in the Zemgale constituency. Latvia's Central Election Commission said that because candidate lists had already been formally submitted, Uzulnieks would remain on the ballot despite his expulsion from the party. ZZS said it would remove campaign materials featuring him. https://www.indiablooms.com/news/india-g.text: News India gets fresh push for permanent UNSC seat as 4 European nations back bid India’s push for a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council received fresh backing on Monday from four European nations — Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic. Speaking to reporters after a meeting between foreign ministers of the Visegrád Group (V4) and India in New York, Slovak Foreign Minister Juraj Blanár said: “We all agree as V4 countries that India, as a part of the Global South, an upcoming superpower in the Indo-Pacific region, must be at the table as the permanent member of the UN Security Council.” ‘We all agree as V4 countries that India as a part of the Global South, upcoming superpower in the Indo-Pacific region, must be at the table as the permanent member of the UN Security Council’ - Foreign Minister Juraj Blanár of Slovakia after the first V4 + India FMM #UNGA81 … pic.twitter.com/QwFsjlXWYC The meeting was held on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly under Slovakia’s presidency of the V4. It marked the first high-level V4-India foreign ministers’ meeting. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar participated in the meeting along with Blanár; Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski; Czech Foreign Minister Petr Macinka; and Hungarian Deputy Foreign Minister Anita Orbán. The ministers discussed ways to strengthen engagement between India and the Visegrád Group. “They acknowledged the strong bilateral relations that exist between India and each of the V4 countries, and noted the potential for the V4+India format to complement and add further momentum to these ties,” the Ministry of External Affairs said in a statement. The discussions covered opportunities for cooperation in areas including trade and investment, technology and innovation, resilient supply chains, defence and security, connectivity, education, mobility and people-to-people exchanges. The ministers also discussed ways to increase interaction among businesses, academic and research institutions and other stakeholders from India and the V4 member states. They exchanged views on global and regional developments, peace and security, as well as cooperation in multilateral forums. The discussions also focused on the need for reformed multilateralism and efforts to address contemporary global challenges, including those affecting the Global South. Jaishankar said the meeting marked a new chapter in India’s engagement with the four Central European countries, with the sides also agreeing to hold annual foreign ministers’ meetings and explore an annual business forum.
